q2: SELECT alias1.c1, alias1.min_price, t5.c1 FROM (SELECT t2.c1, MIN(t5.c3) AS min_price FROM t2 LEFT JOIN t5 ON t2.c1 = t5.c2 GROUP BY t2.c1) AS alias1 NATURAL JOIN t5;
explanation: Q1 computes the minimum t5.c3 per t5.c2 and LEFT joins t2 to those minima, then LEFT joins to t5 on (t2.c1 = t5.c2 AND t5.c3 = min_price). Q2 first computes the same minima per t2.c1, but then NATURAL JOINs with t5 on the common column name c1, i.e., alias1.c1 = t5.c1. Thus Q2 joins on t5.c1 (not t5.c2) and is an inner join, potentially dropping rows and/or matching unrelated t5 rows, whereas Q1 joins on t5.c2 and enforces the min-price match.
counterexample_dsp: Have one t2 row with c1 = 'A'. Add t5 rows whose c2 = 'A' but whose c1 are 'X' and 'Y' (different from 'A'), with prices 5.00 and 7.00. Q1 returns ('A', 5.00, 'X'). Q2 NATURAL JOINs on c1, looking for t5.c1 = 'A', finds none, and returns no rows.
